about:
# CompassHUD

A configurable compass strip that displays your character's heading, along with various markers with information such as name, distance, and time to arrival.

![Example1](https://i.imgur.com/NmushPm.png)

## Inspirations

I was inspired by [Compass](https://www.wowinterface.com/downloads/info14051-Compass.html) and [GoWCompass](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/gowcompass).
While influenced by their ideas, I wrote my own code from scratch—avoiding too much copy-paste.

## Main Features

- Fully movable and resizable compass strip.
- Optional numeric heading display.
- Ready-made looks for the whole compass (try them live, keep or revert), and looks shared as text.
- Support for predefined or custom compass textures, or a strip built from configurable letters and degree marks.
- Plethora of markers to be displayed on the compass:
  - the quest, map pin, POI or vignette you are tracking (supertracking), each quest type with its own look,
  - your corpse while you are a ghost,
  - TomTom's crazy arrow target and all your TomTom waypoints,
  - minimap icons (flight points, area POIs, delves, events, dungeon entrances, vignettes, world quests, quests from your quest log, ...),
  - party and raid members,
  - gathering nodes from GatherMate2 (or GatherLite in WoW: Forever),
  - Questie's minimap icons: available quests, turn-ins, objectives, townsfolk (innkeepers, trainers, mailboxes, ...),
  - the icons of HandyNotes plugins (MapNotes, treasures and rares of the expansion plugins, your own notes, ...).
- Name, distance (yards or meters) and time to arrival for markers.
- Profiles for different characters or setups.

### Some examples:

*- Changing background and border:*
![BackgroundBorder](https://i.imgur.com/fKY6J1S.png)

*- Configuring compass HUD FOV (up to 360°):*
![FOV](https://i.imgur.com/Q9HEzRG.png)

*- Allowing quest markers to remain visible on the edge of the compass HUD:*
![QuestOutOfBoundery](https://i.imgur.com/jzSYOS6.png)

*- Customizing visibility, textures, and behavior for various pointer types:*
![CustomTextures](https://i.imgur.com/fhRaRWj.png)

*- Setting numerical heading display options:*
![Heading](https://i.imgur.com/CxlBmpL.png)

*- Questie's icons (quest givers, turn-ins, townsfolk) on the compass:*
![QuestieInAction](https://i.imgur.com/hJeXf5u.png)

## Configuration

Find the `CompassHUD` addon in the `Options` -> `AddOns` section of the game menu. It has the main page and the `Supertracker`, `Minimap tracking` and `Profiles` subpages. The AddOns compartment entry (and the optional minimap button) opens the settings too: left-click in a window you can drag away from the compass, right-click in the game's settings.

Most settings have a tooltip with more details when you hover over them.

### HUD settings

- The `General` tab contains basic global settings:
  - lock the compass in place (it can still be moved in the game's Edit Mode: drag the highlighted compass, click it to open these options), show the minimap button and the AddOns compartment entry,
  - distances in yards or meters, and optionally as whole numbers (distances under 1000 otherwise show one decimal),
  - update frequency, field of view, scale, width and height (in percent, or in pixels with `Size by: Pixels`), marker scale (all markers, separate from the compass size) and frame strata,
  - `Visibility State`: a macro condition deciding when the HUD is shown (default `[petbattle] hide; show`); the HUD is always hidden in instances where the game gives no player facing (dungeons, raids),
  - center the HUD horizontally or reset its position.

![Settings](https://i.imgur.com/wym5Vc0.png)

*The compass in the game's Edit Mode (drag it to move, click it for the options):*
![EditMode](https://i.imgur.com/pf4eOgR.png)

- The `Looks` tab has ready-made looks for the whole compass: frame, letters, fonts, colors and pointer textures, each with a picture. A look never changes the compass size, position or what it shows.
  - `Try` shows a look on the compass right away; then `Keep` it or `Revert` to the look you had, in the same row.
  - Looks: `Clean`, `Fade`, `Horizon`, `Glass`, `Line`, `Night`, `Classic gold`, `Classic gold, fading`, `Gilded`, `Forever`, `Forever, no frame`, `ElvUI` and `EllesmereUI` (shown when that addon is loaded, with its font and colors), and `Original` (CompassHUD's look on a fresh install, also undoes your look changes).
  - `Your own look`: `Restore` brings back the look you had before you first tried one, even after `Keep`. `Export` shows your current look as text to share or keep; `Import` tries a look someone shared. Only the look is shared.
  - `Preview background` puts a plain background (snow, sand, sky, grass, stone, night, ...) behind the compass, to see how a look reads on different surroundings. It is not saved.
  - Tweak a look further in the other tabs.

![Looks](https://i.imgur.com/1GSQnvs.png)

- The `Appearance` tab styles the HUD frame (central pin, opacity, border, background, edge line). `Fade toward the edges` fades the compass and everything on it out toward the left and right edge: where the fading starts, the opacity before fading and at the edge, how it fades, and which parts fade (background and border, compass, edge lines, minimap tracking, supertracker, party/raid, markers held at the edge). Its `Pointer font` section sets a default font, size, outline and color for all pointer texts. A text with its own custom font enabled keeps using that one. Party/raid names keep their own color setting. `Max title width` cuts off long titles of the supertracker pointers and of all icon markers with "..." (0 = no limit).

- The `Custom HUD` tab lets you choose between the compass texture or a strip built from its parts: main cardinal directions (N, E, S, W), ordinal directions (NE, SE, ...) and degrees, each with its own font, color and position. It also holds the numeric heading display (frame, font, decimal points, north shown as 0 or 360).

![Custom](https://i.imgur.com/ElQIDGp.png)

- The `Speech` tab (accessibility) reads out the name of what is in front of you on the compass, with the game's text to speech: the supertracked target, TomTom's crazy arrow target, minimap icons, Questie icons, gathering nodes, TomTom waypoints and/or HandyNotes icons (the one closest to the direction you are facing), each with its own toggle, optionally with the distance. Each one is read once, when you turn to it and have faced it for a short delay; you can set the facing angle, the delay, the voice (any voice the game offers), rate and volume, and test it. `Only read out names shown on the compass` limits it to what currently shows its name (with a texts visibility angle: the one icon showing its texts). Text to speech is played outside the game's sound channels, so it has its own volume.

![Speech](https://i.imgur.com/GxYMsDN.png)

- The `Glow` tab makes the compass glow while you are inside the area of a quest (the highlighted area on the map), so you see you have arrived without opening the map. It is on by default. The supertracked quest and your other watched quests each have their own color, size, inset (how far the glow also reaches into the compass, fading inward), intensity and pulsing (the others can use the supertracked quest's look). After a number of seconds inside, the glow eases down to a weaker one, so you still know you are in the area. The game only tells whether you are inside the area of a watched (tracked) quest. With Questie, its icon themes `Questie` and `pfQuest` switch the game's quest areas off, so the glow cannot work; `Keep the game's quest areas on with Questie` (shown only with Questie loaded) keeps them on, at the price of the game's own quest markers showing next to Questie's icons. The look of the glow is part of the looks.

### Supertracker

Under the `Supertracker` submenu, you can configure visibility and behavior for the pointers to what you are tracking.

*General behavior settings:*
![PointerGeneral](https://i.imgur.com/qWe8KPX.png)

- `Pointers stay on HUD`: a pointer outside the field of view stays at the edge of the HUD (optionally with an out-of-HUD indicator).
- `Hide pointers to other continents`.
- `Use map transition for pointers`: when the target is in another zone, point to the way there suggested by the map (portal, entrance, ...).

*Choosing from pointer texture presets:*
![PointerPresets](https://i.imgur.com/V1mzqaP.png)

There is a pointer type for each kind of target: your corpse (while you are a ghost), user map pin, POI map pin, quest classifications (Quest, Campaign, Important, Legendary, Questline, Meta, Calling, Bonus, Threat, World Quest), daily, weekly and scheduled quests, and an "unknown" fallback. The pointer for TomTom's crazy arrow has the same settings, on the TomTom page under `Minimap tracking` (see Addon integrations).

*For each pointer type, you can also customize:*
*- Visibility, position, size, and textures (separately for a quest in progress and ready to turn in)*
*- Edge detection and rotation (mainly for arrow textures)*
*- Dynamic icon replacements (for World Quests, POI map pins, etc.)*
*- In-game SuperTracker retexturing (the game's diamond above the target uses the pointer's texture)*
*- Copying texture or text settings from another pointer type*

![PointerTexts](https://i.imgur.com/a9x1IA8.png)

*Text display options with font and size selection:*
![PointerTextures](https://i.imgur.com/hUQFmd7.png)

### Minimap tracking

Under the `Minimap tracking` submenu, you'll find settings for icons usually shown on the minimap. These modules can display many icons on the HUD, which costs some performance when everything is enabled.

#### Minimap icons

The `Minimap icons` section covers standard WoW minimap icons (off by default). It has four tabs:
- `General`: scanning radius, update throttle, position, scale, and an opacity gradient based on distance.
- `Filter`: which icon types are shown, in sub-tabs. Each type has `Any distance` next to it (shown regardless of the scanning radius: everything the game lists for the current map, for flight points this can be the whole continent). `Places`: one row per type. `Quests`: quests from your quest log that have a place on the current map (objective area, or the turn-in when complete), with `Progress` (all, in progress or ready to turn in), optionally only those of the zone you are in, with the supertracker's icons or the game's quest marks. `Flight points` hides the other faction's ones and can show only the closest one. `World quests` can be filtered to none, all, tracked ones or those tracked by World Quest Tracker.
- `Texts`: name, distance and time to arrival, shown for all icons or only for the one you're facing (`Texts visibility angle`). With an angle set here or in the other icon sections (gathering nodes, Questie, TomTom, HandyNotes), only one icon of them all shows its texts: the one closest to the direction you are facing.
- `Supertracking`: a keybind that sets the icon you are facing as the game's tracked target (press again to clear it), `Hide icon at the tracked target` (on by default: while an icon is tracked, only its supertracker pointer is shown), and the texture used when a user waypoint has to be created. A waypoint keeps the icon's name, and with `Icon texture` its icon. The other icon sections can use the same keybind (`Use supertracker keybinding` in their sections); for TomTom waypoints it makes the waypoint you face the crazy arrow's target.

*Filter tab, `Places` and `Quests`:*
![MinimapIconsPlaces](https://i.imgur.com/AyYAzuF.png)
![MinimapIconsQuests](https://i.imgur.com/avo0S4y.png)

#### Party/Raid

In the `Party/Raid` section, you can configure the visibility of party and raid members, including icon textures, name display (class colors, fonts, backgrounds), and formatting.
(Default: Party only)

Members on a different map (another continent, behind a portal, underground, ...) can get their own marker style; their direction may not be accurate.

#### Addon integrations

Each addon has its own section under `Minimap tracking`, shown when the addon is loaded. They all work the same way: off by default; the Minimap icons settings (scanning radius, update throttle, position, scale, opacity, texts) or, with `Use minimap icons settings` off, their own; a texts visibility angle; and optionally the supertrack keybinding and text to speech for the icon you face.

- **GatherMate2 / GatherLite**: possible gathering node locations within a scanning radius. Node types follow GatherMate2's own display filter. In WoW: Forever, `GatherLite` works the same way when GatherMate2 is not loaded, following GatherLite's minimap tracking toggles. Unlike the others, it has its own settings by default.
- **HandyNotes**: the icons HandyNotes plugins place on the minimap: MapNotes, the treasures and rares of the expansion plugins, your own notes, and so on.
  - `Plugins`: which plugins appear on the compass (all by default). Plugins turned off in HandyNotes are not shown either.
  - `Icons from nearby zones` (off by default): also the icons of zones and cities around you within the scanning radius. Off, only the icons of the zone you are in are shown, as on HandyNotes' minimap.
  - Names come from the plugins' own data where they provide it (MapNotes, the expansion plugins of Zarillion and Kemayo, your own notes); other icons are titled with the plugin's name.
  - The supertrack keybinding sets a map waypoint on the icon you face.
- **Questie** (experimental): the icons Questie places on the minimap: available quests, quest turn-ins, quest objectives and the townsfolk chosen in Questie's minimap menu. Which icons appear is decided by Questie's own settings. The name can show the kind of icon in parentheses, e.g. "Innkeeper Farley (Innkeeper)". The supertrack keybinding tracks the quest itself for turn-ins and objectives, else it sets a waypoint with the icon's name and look. Questie has no public interface for its icons, so a Questie update may turn this off until CompassHUD is updated.
- **TomTom**: your TomTom waypoints, and the crazy arrow's target as a pointer.
  - Waypoints are shown with the icon of TomTom's minimap theme. `Waypoints from other zones` (on by default) also shows those set on other maps of the continent you are on, e.g. in the zone around a city. `Any distance` (on by default) shows them beyond the scanning radius, fading to the minimum opacity. The crazy arrow's waypoint is not shown twice.
  - The supertrack keybinding makes the waypoint you face the crazy arrow's target. Pressed while facing the crazy arrow's waypoint, it clears the arrow (the waypoint stays in TomTom).
  - `Crazy arrow` tab: the arrow's pointer, with the same settings as the supertracker's pointer types (textures, texts, position). `Hide duplicate TomTom pointer` (on by default) shows only the game's pointer when the arrow's waypoint is at the same place as what the game is tracking. `Use text to speech` reads out the arrow's waypoint. `Use TomTom's arrow` (off by default) uses the arrow of TomTom's minimap theme instead of the pointer textures; it points at the compass, and sideways toward the waypoint when the pointer stays at the compass edge. The pointer follows TomTom's arrow: it goes away when the arrow is cleared, and hides while TomTom hides it (e.g. when the waypoint is on another continent).
- **World Quest Tracker**: its tracked quests can be used as the world quest filter for minimap icons.

*Questie icons on the compass, and their settings:*
![QuestieInAction](https://i.imgur.com/hJeXf5u.png)
![QuestieSettings](https://i.imgur.com/qHnkZhv.png)

### Miscellaneous

#### Custom compass strip textures
You can use your own.

It must be 2048x16, have 720 degrees starting from N(orth), and be in BLP or TGA format (see `CompassHUD.tga` in the Media folder for reference).

Save your file somewhere in the `Interface\Addons` folder (outside any addon folder to avoid deletion on update).

In your SavedVariables file located at `WTF\Account\<AccountID>\SavedVariables\CompassHUD.lua`, add:
*`CompassTextureTexture = [[Interface\Addons\]] .. {your file name without extension}`*
just after the line containing:
*`["PositionX"]`*

Check that you put it in the correct profile. Edit the file only while the game is closed (or logged out), as the game overwrites it on logout.

## For addon authors

Your addon can show its own markers on the compass (with names, distances, the supertrack keybinding, text to speech and a settings page of their own) through CompassHUD's interface: see [docs/API.md](https://github.com/BelegCufea/CompassHUD/blob/master/docs/API.md), with a complete example addon.

## Issues and suggestions

If you run into problems or have feature requests, feel free to [open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/BelegCufea/CompassHUD/issues).

releases.notes:
## New

- **Glow inset in the looks** (`Options → Looks`): the ready-made looks now set a glow inset, so the glow no longer ends in a hard cut at the compass edge: 10 pixels for the looks without a frame (`Fade`, `Line`, `Horizon`, `Gilded`, `Forever, no frame`), where the cut was most visible, and 6 for the looks with a border. It is applied when you try or keep a look; the glow of your own settings stays as you set it until then.

## Fixed

- **Glow left on after an instance**: when the compass hides in an instance, the glow is cleared too, so it is not still on when the compass shows again.
- **Compass back in the centre after a reload** (reported by [Karge](https://www.curseforge.com/members/karge)): when the game had not placed the compass yet as its settings were applied, an empty position was saved, which put the compass back in the centre on the next login or reload. Such a position is no longer saved, and a compass moved right up to the left or bottom edge of the screen no longer counts as never placed.

## New

- **Glow with Questie** (`Options → Glow → Keep the game's quest areas on with Questie`, only shown while Questie is loaded, off by default; suggested by [senrik](https://github.com/senrik)): Questie's icon themes `Questie` and `pfQuest` switch the game's own quest areas off, so there was no area for the glow to react to (only the `Blizzard` theme left them on). With this option the game's quest areas stay on, so the glow works with Questie's icons. The game's own quest markers then also appear on the map and minimap next to Questie's icons. The setting is only written when you switch the option, at login and after you change Questie's icon theme; switching the option off puts back what Questie's theme wants. Nothing is touched without Questie.
- **Glow inset** (`Options → Glow`, for both looks, default 0): how far the glow also reaches inward. The glow stays strongest at the compass's edge and fades out on both sides, outward by `Size` and inward by `Inset`, which looks softer on a compass with a thin line or border along the edge. With 0 it only reaches outward, as before.

## New

- **Glow in quest areas (new, on by default):** the compass now glows while you are inside the area of a quest, the highlighted area on the map that shows where a quest's objectives are. You see you have arrived without opening the map. The glow fades in when you enter the area and fades out when you leave. After 5 seconds inside it eases down to a weaker glow (not off), so you still know you are in the area without it staying distracting. This is a new feature that is on in every profile, including existing ones; to turn it off, untick `Options → Glow → Glow inside quest areas`.
  - It glows for the supertracked quest (gold) and for your other watched quests (cyan). The game only tells whether you are inside the area of a watched (tracked) quest, so quests you do not track cannot glow. You can turn the other watched quests off, or let them use the supertracked quest's look with `Same as Supertracked`.
  - Each of the two has its own color, size, intensity and pulsing. `Ease off after` and `Ease down to` set when and how far the glow eases down (0 seconds keeps it at full strength). The glow follows `Fade toward the edges` for the background and border.
  - The look of the glow is part of the looks (`Options → Looks`): each ready-made look has glow colors that fit its style, and shared looks carry them. Whether the glow is on, which quests it covers and the easing stay as you set them. (Requested in #27.)
- **Corpse pointer:** while you are a ghost, a pointer shows the way to your corpse, like the one for a tracked quest: it stays on the compass at the edge when the corpse is out of sight, with its distance and the time to get there, and is read out with the supertracked target. It is a pointer type of its own (`Options → Supertracker → Pointers → Corpse`), so its look, size and texts can be set or the pointer turned off. (Requested in #26.)

## New

- **Fade toward the edges** (`Options → Appearance`): the compass and everything on it fades out toward the left and right edge, on its own or with the `CompassHUD gradient` background. Set where the fading starts, the opacity before fading and at the edge, and how it fades (even, slow then faster, fast then slower, slow at both ends). Choose what fades: the background and border, the compass (texture, or the custom compass' letters, degrees and ticks), the edge lines, minimap tracking, the supertracker and party/raid. `Also markers held at the edge` fades the supertracker and party/raid markers that stay at the edge while their target is outside the field of view; turn it off to keep them at full opacity.
- **New looks** with the fading on (`Options → Looks`): `Horizon` (no frame, letters between two thin lines on a faint dark band, all fading away to the sides), `Glass` (a dark band with a thin border, the whole compass fading out) and `Classic gold, fading`.

## Fix

- **While you are dead:** a flight point, map pin, rare (vignette) or waypoint you track was not shown as the supertracker pointer (only your corpse and quests were), and the supertracker keybinding could not untrack it. They now show next to your corpse.
- **Supertracker keybinding:** after moving to another map, it sometimes did nothing on a minimap icon you faced (e.g. a flight point, after stepping out of the Deeprun Tram into Ironforge) until a /reload. Icons that the game lists on several maps (flight points, quests next to your zone) kept the map they were first seen on, and the keybinding skipped them. They now belong to the map you are on.

## Good to know

- **Minimap button / broker / AddOn compartment:** left-click now opens the options in a movable window. The game's settings page opens with **right-click**.
- **TomTom waypoints** (if you show them on the compass) now appear at any distance, not only within the scanning radius. Turn off `Minimap tracking → TomTom → Any distance` to hide far ones again.

## New

- **Looks** tab (`Options → Looks`): ready-made looks for the whole compass (frame, letters, fonts, colors, pointer textures), each with a picture. `Try` shows one on the compass right away, then `Keep` it or `Revert` to the look you had, right in its row. A look never changes the compass size, position or what it shows.
  - Looks: `Clean` (flat and dark), `Fade` (no frame, a band fading to both sides), `Line` (no frame or background, a line on top), `Night`, `Classic gold`, `Gilded` (gold lines, no frame), `Forever` and `Forever, no frame` (dark leather, copper and antique gold), `ElvUI` / `EllesmereUI` (shown when that addon is loaded, with its font and colors), and `Original` (CompassHUD's look on a fresh install, also undoes your look changes).
  - `Preview background` (snow, sand, sky, grass, stone, night, ...) shows a plain background behind the compass and its markers, to check how a look reads on different surroundings. It is not saved.
  - `Your own look → Export` shows your current look as text in a window, to copy and share or keep; `Import` takes a look someone shared and tries it (`Keep` / `Revert` as with the other looks). Only the look is shared, never size, position or what the compass shows.
  - `Your own look → Restore` brings back the look you had before you first tried one, even after `Keep`.

  ![Looks](https://i.imgur.com/1GSQnvs.png)
- **Minimap button / broker / AddOn compartment:** left-click opens the options in a window you can drag away from the compass (click again to close it), right-click in the game's settings as before.
- **TomTom waypoints:** `Any distance` (on by default) shows them beyond the scanning radius, as TomTom's minimap does with its edge arrows, also when using the minimap icons settings. Far ones fade to the minimum opacity.
- **TomTom:** the supertracker keybinding now also clears the crazy arrow: press it while facing the TomTom pointer (at any distance). The waypoint stays in TomTom and shows as a marker again, as with `Clear waypoint from arrow` in TomTom's menu.

## Misc

- New libraries for sharing looks as text: AceSerializer-3.0 (Ace3 r1284) and LibDeflate (1.0.2).

## *For developers only*

- *Other addons can show their markers on the compass: `CompassHUD.RegisterMarkerSource`, documented in [docs/API.md](https://github.com/BelegCufea/CompassHUD/blob/master/docs/API.md) with an example addon. CompassHUD's own TomTom, Questie, HandyNotes and gathering markers use it too.*
- *The compass frame is now called `CompassHUDFrame` (it was `CompassHUD`), e.g. for anchoring to it in WeakAuras or a layout addon. `CompassHUD` is now the addon's interface for other addons.*
